attempts.transport_diagnostic: You've hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Sep 14th, 2026 9:22 PM.

concern_results.conclusion: Traced the classification chain in the diff: extraction reads only top-level error/*.failed events (message or error.message), the added `usage limit` pattern and the $TRANSPORT_ERRORS input reach the existing quota and auth predicates without reordering them, and every stub fixture maps to its asserted verdict (usage_limit_event and usage_limit_turn_failed to quota/true, auth_event to provider_unavailable/true, quota_in_model_output to unknown_client_failure/false); acceptance rows A1-A11 each have a corresponding executable assertion.

The diagnostic is built only from the transport's top-level events and stderr, and the redaction sequence in the diff (run-root and HOME replacement, URL query strip before key=value strip, sk-/Bearer/JWT/assignment patterns) removes every sensitive shape the sensitive_streams fixture emits, including the compound access_token=/client_secret= and quoted JSON refresh_token forms; the credential scanner conflict was handled by assembling the fixture value at runtime rather than weakening the redaction.

Empty or unreadable $EVENTS exits the extractor softly to an empty file, the builder falls back from transport errors to the stderr tail with tail-truncation (keeping the line that names the cause, verified by the long_stderr marker row), and a completely silent failure still yields the non-empty "no transport output captured" fallback placed outside the builder so builder failure is covered; head-vs-tail truncation direction is chosen by keep_head correctly for both sources.

The eight new behavior rows fail against the unchanged wrapper for the reason each names, and the four single-predicate mutations (raw-stream read, no redaction, no bound, stderr-only grep) each red exactly the rows that predicate protects, so the containment claims are executed rather than asserted; the two rows green on baseline by construction (model-output refusal, success-path key absence) derive their meaning from those mutations, and green-suite plus make test plus the heavy lane are recorded as passing.

emit_inconclusive's new sixth positional defaults to empty so all pre-existing call sites produce byte-identical receipts, no flag, exit code, or reason code changed, the success path adds no key, and the Bash 3.2 hazard (heredoc inside command substitution broken by a comment apostrophe) was removed by writing through a file rather than patched locally, with /bin/bash -n and the existing 3.2 compatibility test green.

The change is additive within one wrapper plus tests and one appended register row; revert restores prior behavior with no persisted state, no migration, and the single new receipt key is relayed uninterpreted by review_gate.py, so no consumer contract needs unwinding.

This is the defect being repaired: previously the EXIT trap deleted both streams and the receipt held only transport_exit_code, leaving the packet-size hypothesis unfalsifiable; now every exit taken after a non-zero run, including classified and silent ones, carries a bounded single-line diagnostic of what the transport said, verified end-to-end against the live quota condition.

The shared-gate failure semantics are contained at both new crossings: the classifier input is restricted to top-level transport events so packet-quoted quota vocabulary nested under item cannot steer the cascade decision (mutation-proven), and the receipt-bound diagnostic is bounded to 600 chars and redacted at build time before it rounds commit as evidence (mutation-proven); CANDIDATE_LOCAL_CODES and every existing reason code's meaning are unchanged.
